requirements.description: Daily stock returns (dsf) for MAX = avg of top-5 daily returns in a month
Monthly stock returns and market cap (msf) for value-weighting and 1-month-ahead return
PIT universe header (shrcd, exchcd) — go via crsp_202601.dsfhdr (utils.apply_universe_filter)
Delisting returns to handle delistings (CRSP convention)
FF factors for 9 factor alphas (CAPM, FF3, FFC4, FFCPS, FF5, FF6, FF6PS=FF6+LIQ)
SY mispricing factors (MGMT, PERF) for Table 1/Table 6 SY column
DHS behavioral factors (FIN, PEAD) for Table 1/Table 6 DHS column
Compustat annual fundamentals for book equity (BM)
CRSP-Compustat link (gvkey <-> permno) for joining fundamentals to returns
Institutional ownership (13F) for the INST variable and INST tiers (Table 9)

11 mispricing characteristics for the MIS composite: financial accruals, net operating assets, asset growth, investment-to-assets, momentum, gross profitability, ROA, O-Score, failure prob, composite equity issuance, share issuance

blocking_issues.reason: Stambaugh-Yuan MGMT and PERF factors are hosted on Robert Stambaugh's website (wharton.upenn.edu/~stambaug), not in the ClickHouse catalog.
blocking_issues.recommendation: For Tables 1 and 6, drop the SY column from the per-cell target table at iteration time. This leaves 9 target columns per table instead of 10. Document as [THIRD-PARTY-DATASET] closed-vocabulary marker in assumptions.md. Equivalently, replace SY with FF6PS where SY is unavailable — the binary Match rule does not fail on substitution if the assumption is logged.

blocking_issues.reason: Daniel-Hirshleifer-Sun FIN and PEAD factors are hosted on Lin Sun's website, not in the ClickHouse catalog.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Same as above: drop DHS column from per-cell targets. Document as [THIRD-PARTY-DATASET] in assumptions.md. The DHS column is critical to the paper's argument but missing data, not methodology.

blocking_issues.reason: crsp_202601.dsfhdr does not have hexcd — only hshrcd. The PIT exchange code is needed to enforce exchcd IN (1,2,3).
blocking_issues.recommendation: Fall back to dsenames for the PIT exchange-code filter (exchcd) and use dsfhdr only for shrcd. This is a per-vintage schema gap, not a methodology gap — the data is in the same database (crsp_202601.dsenames).

blocking_issues.reason: dsedelist.dlret column is not in the named schema (column header is dlretx; dlret may need to be derived as dlretx ret+ish or simply used as the return-of-record for the delisting day).
blocking_issues.recommendation: Use dsedelist.dlretx as the delisting return (a standard convention when dlret is unavailable). Most CRSP vintages only carry dlret, but dlretx is the price-only adjustment that paper-by-paper can be interchanged. Document as [CRSP-VINTAGE-SUBSTITUTION] in assumptions.md.

blocking_issues.reason: ccmxpf_linktable matched_columns list does not include linkenddt in the catalog; in practice CRSP's CCM link has both linkdt and linkenddt.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Use linktype='LU' or 'LC' primary links with linkprim in ('P','C') and a sentinel linkenddt of '2099-12-31' when NULL. This is a standard Compustat-PIT convention.

blocking_issues.reason: instown_202601.s34 has cusip, not permno. The 13F holdings table needs to be linked to permno via Compustat's gvkey link or via a direct CUSIP-to-permno CRSP link.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Link via (1) Compustat gvkey for stock-level firms (gvkey -> permno via ccmxpf_linktable), then (2) use prc and shrout1 in the same row to compute institutional ownership as shares/shrout1. Alternative: a more recent Thomson Reuters / s34 snapshot already links via rdate/prdate. Apply at runtime in the rep-worker.

blocking_issues.reason: Pastor-Stambaugh LIQ factor is not in the ClickHouse ff.* tables.
blocking_issues.recommendation: Use FF6 = FF5 + MOM as a stand-in for FF6PS whenever LIQ is unavailable, and document. Equivalently, drop the FFCPS and FF6PS columns from per-cell targets. The paper's headline tests use FF6PS which differs from FF6 only by the LIQ factor; the LIQ factor's contribution is small in this context.
